nodes.title: Each environment teaches one named RL concept, and I can explain, backed by my own runs, why the agent learns.
Algorithms I write from scratch are trustworthy: on the same environment, they perform about as well as a well-known library version.
Every trained agent clearly beats both a random player and a simple scripted player, measured over many games rather than judged by eye.
I can watch a replay of any trained agent playing.
A new environment reuses a shared core (environment interface, training loop, logging, replay viewer), so it only needs its own game and concept code.
A new game places a length-3 snake and one food on a 10×10 grid.

criteria: Given a new game, when it starts, then the snake has length 3, lies fully inside the grid, and the food is on a cell the snake does not occupy.

nodes.title: Each step takes one of three actions: go straight, turn left, or turn right, relative to the current heading.

criteria: Given the snake heading up, when the action is "turn left", then the head moves one cell left and the heading becomes left.

nodes.title: Moving onto the food grows the snake by 1 and adds 1 to the score.

criteria: Given the head next to the food, when it moves onto it, then length and score each increase by 1, and new food appears on an empty cell.

nodes.title: Moving into a wall or the snake's own body ends the game.

criteria: Given the head at the right edge heading right, when the action is "go straight", then the game is over.
Given the head next to its own body, when it moves into the body, then the game is over.

nodes.title: A game ends after 100 × current length steps without eating.

criteria: Given a length-3 snake that has not eaten for 299 steps, when it takes one more step without eating, then the game is over.

nodes.title: Rewards default to +1 for food, −1 for game over, and 0 otherwise. Each run can set its own values.

criteria: Given default settings, when the snake eats, then the reward is +1. When the game ends by collision or starvation, the reward is −1.
Given a run that sets food to +10, when the snake eats, then the reward is +10.

nodes.title: Games are reproducible from a seed.

criteria: Given the same seed and the same actions, when two games are played, then every snake position, food position and reward is identical.

nodes.title: The compact view gives 11 yes/no values: danger straight, left and right; heading (one of four); and whether the food is left, right, above or below the head.

criteria: Given a wall directly ahead and food above-right of the head, when the compact view is read, then "danger straight", "food right" and "food up" are yes, and the other danger and food values are no.

nodes.title: The full-grid view shows every cell's contents: empty, snake head, snake body, or food.

criteria: Given any game state, when the full-grid view is read, then exactly one cell is marked head, one is marked food, and the body cells match the snake's body.

nodes.title: The tank is a circle of radius 1. The ball (radius 0.08) moves 0.03 per step in a straight line and reflects off the wall at the angle it arrived, at unchanged speed.

criteria: Given the ball heading straight at the wall along a radius, when it reaches the wall, then it comes back along the same radius at speed 0.03.
Given the ball arriving at 30° to the wall's normal, when it reflects, then it leaves at 30° on the other side of the normal.

nodes.title: Each fish's action is a 2-D swim vector. A vector longer than 1 is shortened to length 1, then scaled by the fish's top speed of 0.024 per step (0.8 × the ball's speed).

criteria: Given the action (3, 4), when the fish moves, then it moves 0.024 in direction (0.6, 0.8).
Given the action (0.5, 0), when the fish moves, then it moves 0.012 in direction (1, 0).

nodes.title: A fish can't leave the tank. A move that would cross the wall stops at the wall.

criteria: Given a fish 0.01 inside the wall swimming straight outward at full speed, when it moves, then it ends on the wall, not beyond it.

nodes.title: A fish is caught when its centre comes within 0.11 of the ball's centre (ball radius 0.08 plus fish radius 0.03). It stops swimming, and its survival time is the number of steps it completed.

criteria: Given a fish 0.10 from the ball's centre after a step, when the step resolves, then that fish is caught with survival time equal to that step's number minus 1.

nodes.title: Each fish earns +1 for each step it survives and 0 on the step it is caught. Each run can set its own values.

criteria: Given default settings, when a fish survives a step, then its reward is +1.

nodes.title: A game ends when every fish is caught or after 1,000 steps. The game's score is the mean survival time per fish.

criteria: Given 8 fish of which 6 are caught at steps 100–600 and 2 survive, when step 1,000 is reached, then the game is truncated and the score is the mean of the 8 survival times, counting 1,000 for each survivor.

nodes.title: The number of fish is set per run, from 1 to 16; the school rungs use 8. Fish never collide and may overlap.

criteria: Given two fish swimming to the same point, when they arrive, then both occupy it and neither is blocked.

nodes.title: A new game places the ball at a random position with a random direction, and each fish at a random position at least 0.4 from the ball. The same seed and actions give the same game.

criteria: Given the same seed and the same actions, when two games are played, then every fish and ball position and every reward is identical.

nodes.title: The full view gives each fish 8 values: its own position and velocity, the ball's position relative to it, and the ball's velocity.

criteria: Given a fish at (0.5, 0) and the ball at (0, 0) moving (0.03, 0), when the fish's full view is read, then the ball's relative position is (−0.5, 0) and its velocity (0.03, 0).

nodes.title: The limited view gives each fish 9 values: its own position and velocity, a "ball visible" flag, and the ball's relative position and velocity. The ball counts as visible only within 0.5 of the fish; otherwise the flag is 0 and the ball values are 0. Fish never see other fish.

criteria: Given the ball 0.6 from a fish, when its limited view is read, then the flag and the four ball values are 0.
Given the ball 0.4 from the fish, when its limited view is read, then the flag is 1 and the ball values match the full view.

nodes.title: A game takes place in a tank of radius 1 with 1 predator, 6 prey and 8 pellets, and ends after 1,000 steps.

criteria: Given a new game, when it starts, then there are 1 predator, 6 prey and 8 pellets inside the tank, and step 1,000 truncates it.

nodes.title: Each animal's action is a 2-D swim vector, shortened to length 1 if longer, then scaled by its top speed: 0.024 per step for prey, 0.03 for the predator. Animals stop at the wall, as in FISH-03.

criteria: Given the predator's action (3, 4), when it moves, then it moves 0.03 in direction (0.6, 0.8).
Given a prey's action (3, 4), when it moves, then it moves 0.024 in direction (0.6, 0.8).

nodes.title: A prey whose centre comes within 0.05 of a pellet's centre eats it and earns +1. The pellet reappears at a random spot 20 steps later.

criteria: Given a prey 0.04 from a pellet after a step, when the step resolves, then the prey earns +1, the pellet is gone, and 20 steps later a pellet appears again.

nodes.title: The predator catches a prey whose centre comes within 0.08 of its own, earning +1 while the prey earns −5. A caught prey is out for 50 steps, then reappears at a random spot at least 0.4 from the predator.

criteria: Given a prey 0.07 from the predator after a step, when the step resolves, then the predator earns +1, the prey −5, and the prey is absent for the next 50 steps.
Given a caught prey's 50 steps are over, when it reappears, then it is at least 0.4 from the predator.

nodes.title: Each prey sees 18 values: its own position and velocity; a "visible" flag and the predator's relative position and velocity, only within 0.5; and, for its 3 nearest pellets within 0.5, a "visible" flag and the relative position of each. Anything out of range is 0 with its flag 0.

criteria: Given the predator 0.6 from a prey, when the prey's view is read, then the predator flag and its four values are 0.

nodes.title: The predator sees 19 values: its own position and velocity, and, for its 3 nearest swimming prey within 0.6, a "visible" flag and the relative position and velocity of each.

criteria: Given only one prey within 0.6, when the predator's view is read, then one prey slot is filled and the other two are 0 with their flags 0.

nodes.title: The predator and the prey are two teams. Each team has its own view and its own policy, and a step takes one action per animal from each team.

criteria: Given a step, when both teams act, then the predator's action comes from the predator team's policy and every prey's from the prey team's policy.

nodes.title: The predator's score is catches per game. The prey's score is the mean total reward per prey per game.

criteria: Given a game with 4 catches and prey rewards summing to 12, when it ends, then the predator scores 4 and the prey score 2.0.

nodes.title: A new game places the prey and pellets at random spots at least 0.4 from the predator. The same seed and actions give the same game.

criteria: Given the same seed and the same actions, when two games are played, then every position, reward and catch is identical.

nodes.title: The random player picks each of the three actions with equal chance.

criteria: Given 30,000 random-player steps, when the actions are counted, then each action's share is between 32% and 35%.

nodes.title: The scripted player steps toward the food if that move is safe. Otherwise it takes any safe move. If no move is safe, it goes straight.

criteria: Given food directly ahead and no danger ahead, when the scripted player moves, then it goes straight.
Given food to the left but danger to the left, and the right is safe, when it moves, then it turns right.

nodes.title: Baselines are evaluated with the same protocol as agents (EVAL-01).

criteria: Given an evaluation report, when it is read, then it lists both baselines' scores next to every agent's.

nodes.title: The random swimmer picks each fish's swim vector uniformly from the disc of radius 1.

criteria: Given 30,000 random-swimmer actions, when their lengths are counted, then between 23% and 27% are shorter than 0.5.

nodes.title: The scripted fish swims at full speed directly away from the ball's centre, using the full view.

criteria: Given the ball at (0, 0) and a fish at (0.3, 0.4), when the scripted fish acts, then its action is (0.6, 0.8) at length 1.
Given the ball exactly on the fish's centre, when it acts, then it swims toward the tank's centre or, at the centre, along (1, 0).

nodes.title: The scripted predator swims at full speed toward its nearest visible prey, otherwise toward the tank's centre.

criteria: Given a visible prey at relative position (0.3, 0.4), when the scripted predator acts, then its action is (0.6, 0.8).
Given no visible prey, when it acts at (0.5, 0), then it swims toward (0, 0).

nodes.title: A scripted prey flees at full speed directly away from the predator when it is within 0.3, and otherwise swims at full speed to its nearest visible pellet. With neither, it stays still.

criteria: Given the predator at relative position (0.12, 0.16), when the scripted prey acts, then its action is (−0.6, −0.8).
Given the predator out of range and a pellet at relative position (0.3, 0), when it acts, then its action is (1, 0).

nodes.title: The random predator and random prey draw each swim vector uniformly from the disc of radius 1, as BASE-04 does.

criteria: Given 30,000 random-predator actions, when their lengths are counted, then between 23% and 27% are shorter than 0.5.

nodes.title: The table-based agent keeps one learned value per compact-view situation and action. It updates that value after every step, from the reward plus its estimate of the next situation.

criteria: Given a step that earns +1 food reward, when the agent updates, then the value for that situation and action moves toward the reward.

nodes.title: While training, each agent sometimes takes a random action instead of its best one. That chance falls over training to a set minimum.

criteria: Given a run's exploration settings, when training reaches the end of the decay period, then the random-action rate equals the set minimum.

nodes.title: The compact-view neural agent learns from batches drawn at random from a memory of past steps.

criteria: Given a full memory, when a training batch is drawn, then it holds steps from more than one game.

nodes.title: The compact-view neural agent computes its learning targets from a separate copy of itself. That copy is refreshed only at set intervals.

criteria: Given a refresh interval of N steps, when fewer than N steps have passed since the last refresh, then the target copy is unchanged.

nodes.title: The full-grid neural agent learns from the full-grid view, using the same memory and target-copy behavior as AGENT-03 and AGENT-04.

criteria: Given a full-grid run, when training starts, then the agent receives only the full-grid view, never the compact view.

nodes.title: The lab's own agents, value learners and policy-gradient learners alike, are written from basic array and tensor operations, including automatic gradients. They contain no reinforcement learning library code.

criteria: Given the agents' code, when it is reviewed, then it uses no reinforcement learning library.

nodes.title: During evaluation, agents never explore. Value learners take their best-valued action, and policy learners take their policy's mean action.

criteria: Given an evaluation game, when the agent acts, then no action is random.

nodes.title: The policy maps each observation to a Gaussian over the 2-D swim vector: a mean from a neural network, and a learned spread. Training samples actions from it.

criteria: Given any observation, when the policy acts during training, then the action is drawn from the Gaussian, and its log-probability is available for learning.

nodes.title: The plain policy-gradient agent updates after each batch of whole games. Each action is pushed toward or away from in proportion to the discounted return from that step, normalised within the batch.

criteria: Given a batch where one action led to a higher return than the batch mean, when the agent updates, then that action's log-probability rises.

nodes.title: The clipped policy-gradient agent learns from batches of steps. It estimates each step's advantage with a learned value estimate, then updates for several passes with an objective that clips the policy's change to within 0.2 of its previous probability ratio.

criteria: Given a batch whose new-to-old probability ratio exceeds 1.2 for a step with positive advantage, when the objective is computed, then that step contributes no further gain beyond the 1.2 ratio.

nodes.title: In a school, one shared policy acts for each fish independently from that fish's own view, and every fish's experience trains it.

criteria: Given a school of 8, when one step is taken, then the policy is queried once per swimming fish, and each fish's step enters the same training batch.

nodes.title: Each rung's settings fix its game, fish count, view and agent, so the four rungs are reproducible runs like any other.

criteria: Given the rung-3 settings, when a run starts, then it trains a shared clipped policy-gradient policy on 8 fish with the full view.

nodes.title: Each learning team uses its own clipped policy-gradient agent (PG-03); in a co-learning run both teams learn at once.

criteria: Given a rung-2 run, when it trains, then the predator and prey policies are updated from their own teams' experience only.

nodes.title: Rung 1 is two runs, each training one team against the other team's scripted player.

criteria: Given the rung-1 prey settings, when the run trains, then the predator is the scripted predator throughout.

nodes.title: In rung 3, each game's opponent for a team is the other team's latest policy with probability 0.5, and otherwise one of its saved past generations, chosen uniformly.

criteria: Given 1,000 rung-3 games after generation 5, when the opponents are counted, then the latest policy is chosen in 45%–55% of them, and every earlier generation appears.

nodes.title: A learning run saves each learning team's policy every tenth of its step budget, giving 10 generations per team.

criteria: Given a finished co-learning run, when its record is opened, then each team has 10 numbered generations.

nodes.title: A cross-play table pits every predator generation against every prey generation of a run: 50 games per pairing on held-out seeds, recording both teams' scores.

criteria: Given a co-learning run's 10 generations per team, when cross-play runs, then the table has 100 cells of 50 games each.

nodes.title: Each generation's rating is its mean score against all of the other team's generations in the cross-play table.

criteria: Given a cross-play table, when ratings are computed, then each predator generation's rating is the mean of its row, and each prey generation's the mean of its column.

nodes.title: The fixed panel for a team is the other team's scripted player, its random player, and the final trained policy from the other team's rung-1 run.

criteria: Given the panel for the prey team, when it is listed, then it holds the scripted predator, the random predator and the rung-1 predator.

nodes.title: An evaluation plays 200 games for each of 5 training seeds, on evaluation seeds never used in training. It reports the mean score and its spread. In every environment, scripted and random players are measured the same way.

criteria: Given a trained agent, when it is evaluated, then 1,000 games are played and the report shows the mean score and spread for each seed and overall.

nodes.title: Every agent in every environment significantly beats that environment's random player. This is tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill on the EVAL-01 scores, and passes only if significant at 5% after correcting for the number of comparisons.

criteria: Given Snake's three agents and the random player's scores, when tested, then each agent's corrected result is significant at 5%.
Given the four fish-tank rungs and the random swimmer's scores, when tested, then each rung's corrected result is significant at 5%.
Given each learned predator-prey team and its own side's random player, both playing against the same scripted opposition, when tested, then each corrected result is significant at 5%.

nodes.title: The compact-view neural agent is not significantly worse than the scripted player, tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill at 5% after correction.

criteria: Given both players' EVAL-01 scores, when tested for "agent worse than scripted", then the result is not significant.

nodes.title: At least one agent significantly beats the scripted player, tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill at 5% after correction.

criteria: Given all three agents' EVAL-01 scores, when each is tested against the scripted player, then at least one corrected result is significant.

nodes.title: The report states, as stretch targets that are not pass conditions, whether Snake's full-grid agent beats the scripted player and whether the limited-view school beats the scripted fish.

criteria: Given either agent's scores, when the report is produced, then it shows that test's result and labels it "stretch".

nodes.title: Each agent's learning curve shows evaluation score against training steps, with the two baseline means drawn as reference lines.

criteria: Given a finished run, when its curve is shown, then both baseline lines appear on the same chart.

nodes.title: The full-view clipped rungs (2 and 3) each significantly beat the scripted fish, tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill at 5% after correction.

criteria: Given each rung's and the scripted fish's EVAL-01 scores, when tested, then each corrected result is significant.

nodes.title: The single-fish clipped agent (rung 2) significantly beats the single-fish plain agent (rung 1), with the same step budget and seeds, tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill at 5% after correction.

criteria: Given both rungs' EVAL-01 scores, when tested for "rung 2 greater than rung 1", then the corrected result is significant.

nodes.title: Each rung-1 predator-prey team significantly beats its own side's scripted player against the same scripted opposition, tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill at 5% after correction.

criteria: Given the rung-1 predator and the scripted predator, each against scripted prey, when tested for "learned greater than scripted" on catches, then the corrected result is significant; likewise for the rung-1 prey and scripted prey against the scripted predator.

nodes.title: Each team's rung-3 final policy significantly beats that team's rung-2 final policy against its fixed panel (SELF-07), pooled over the panel's opponents, tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill at 5% after correction.

criteria: Given both rungs' final predators against the predator's panel, when tested for "rung 3 greater than rung 2", then the corrected result is significant; likewise for the prey.

nodes.title: The report shows rung 2's and rung 3's cross-play tables and each team's ratings by generation. Rung 2's are labelled "reported", not a pass condition.

criteria: Given a finished predator-prey report, when it is read, then both rungs' tables and rating charts appear, and rung 2's carry the "reported" label.

nodes.title: For each environment, the reference implementation trains on the compared rung's setup: the same game, view, agent counts, opponent, rewards, number of training steps and training seeds. It is evaluated with EVAL-01.

criteria: Given a reference run, when its settings are compared with the compared rung's, then game, view, fish count, rewards, steps and seeds match.

nodes.title: The compared rung's mean score is at least 90% of the reference's mean score.

criteria: Given both EVAL-01 results, when compared, then agent mean ≥ 0.9 × reference mean.

nodes.title: The compared rung is not significantly worse than the reference, tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill at 5% after correction.

criteria: Given both EVAL-01 score sets, when tested for "agent worse than reference", then the result is not significant.

nodes.title: The compact-view neural agent can run with no memory, learning only from its most recent step.

criteria: Given the no-memory switch, when training, then each update uses only the latest step.

nodes.title: The compact-view neural agent can run with no separate target copy, computing targets from itself.

criteria: Given the no-target-copy switch, when training, then the targets come from the current agent at every step.

nodes.title: The table-based agent can run with no exploration, always taking its best-valued action.

criteria: Given the no-exploration switch, when training, then no action is random.

nodes.title: Each ablation trains with the same seeds and step budget as the full agent. Its learning curve is shown on one chart beside the full agent's.

criteria: Given a finished ablation, when the comparison is shown, then both curves share one chart and the report gives each one's EVAL-01 mean.

nodes.title: A run is fully described by its settings: environment and its own settings (such as fish count), view, agent, rewards, exploration where the agent uses it, step budget and seed.

criteria: Given a settings description, when a run is launched from it, then no other input is needed.

nodes.title: Each run saves its settings, its seed, its learning-curve data, a final checkpoint per learning team, its saved generations when SELF-04 applies, and recorded evaluation games.

criteria: Given a finished run, when its record is opened, then its settings, seed, curve, final checkpoints and recorded games are present.
Given a finished co-learning run, when its record is opened, then each team's 10 generations are present.

nodes.title: The same settings and seed on the same machine produce the same learning curve.

criteria: Given two runs with identical settings and seed, when their curves are compared, then they match exactly.

nodes.title: During training, progress is shown at least every 30 seconds: steps, games, recent mean score, and elapsed time.

criteria: Given a running training job, when 30 seconds pass, then a progress line has appeared.

nodes.title: A saved checkpoint can be reloaded and evaluated without retraining.

criteria: Given a finished run's checkpoint, when it is evaluated, then the scores match the run's own evaluation.

nodes.title: Any recorded game from any saved run can be played back, showing the board (Snake's grid, the corridor, or the tank with the ball and every fish, caught fish marked), the score and the step number.

criteria: Given a saved run, when one of its games is replayed, then each frame matches the recorded game state.

nodes.title: Playback can be paused, stepped one frame at a time, and sped up or slowed down.

criteria: Given a paused replay, when "step" is pressed, then exactly one frame advances.

nodes.title: New games can be recorded from any saved checkpoint, or in predator-prey from any pairing of a predator and a prey checkpoint or generation, and then replayed.

criteria: Given a checkpoint and a seed, when games are recorded, then they can be replayed like any other recorded game.
Given prey generation 2 and predator generation 9 of a run, when a game is recorded, then it replays like any other.

nodes.title: Every environment offers the same two operations, and declares its teams: each team's agents, observation shape, and whether its actions are discrete or continuous. Starting a game from a seed returns one observation per agent of each team. Taking a step, with one action per active agent of each team, returns each agent's next observation and reward, which agents are done, whether the game is over, and extra information.

criteria: Given Snake (one team, one agent, discrete), the fish tank (one team, 8 agents, continuous) or predator-prey (a 1-agent and a 6-agent team, continuous), when a game is started and stepped, then all return the same kinds of result.

nodes.title: Training, logging, evaluation and replay work with any environment that offers CORE-01's interface.

criteria: Given the corridor, when it is trained, evaluated and replayed, then it uses the same training, logging, evaluation and replay as Snake.

nodes.title: The corridor is a row of 10 cells. The agent starts at the left end and moves left or right. Reaching the right end gives +1 and ends the game. A game also ends after 50 steps.

criteria: Given the agent at cell 9 of 10, when it moves right, then the reward is +1 and the game is over.
Given the agent at the left end, when it moves left, then it stays in place.

nodes.title: The table-based agent, trained on the corridor through the core, reaches the right end in ≥ 95% of evaluation games, in at most 12 steps.

criteria: Given a trained corridor agent, when evaluated, then ≥ 95% of games reach the right end within 12 steps.

nodes.title: Adding the corridor needs no change to the shared core.

criteria: Given the core as Snake uses it, when the corridor is added, then the change touches only corridor code.

nodes.title: Snake and the corridor behave exactly as before after the core's interface revision.

criteria: Given a seed and an action sequence recorded before the revision, when they are replayed after it, then every observation, reward and game end is identical.

nodes.title: The fish tank and the predator-prey world train, log, evaluate and replay through the shared core, with no training loop, evaluation or replay of their own.

criteria: Given a fish-tank or predator-prey run, when it is trained, evaluated and replayed, then it uses the same training, logging, evaluation and replay as Snake.

nodes.title: Evaluation games never reuse a seed used in training.

criteria: Given any evaluation, when its seeds are checked against the run's training seeds, then none overlap.

nodes.title: All training and evaluation data comes from the lab's own environments. No outside datasets are used.

criteria: Given any run, when its inputs are listed, then they are only settings and environment output.

nodes.title: Training the table-based Snake agent takes ≤ 10 minutes per seed on the learner's laptop (Apple Silicon, processor only).

criteria: Timed from the run's own elapsed-time log.

nodes.title: Training the compact-view neural agent takes ≤ 60 minutes per seed on the same laptop, processor only.

criteria: Timed from the run's own elapsed-time log.

nodes.title: Training the full-grid neural agent takes ≤ 60 minutes per seed, on the laptop or on rented hardware within QR-05.

criteria: Timed from the run's own elapsed-time log.

nodes.title: Evaluating one agent (EVAL-01, 1,000 games) takes ≤ 5 minutes on the laptop.

criteria: Timed during evaluation.

nodes.title: Rented cloud hardware costs ≤ $5 in total per stage, and is used only when a training-time limit (QR-03, QR-07) can't be met on the laptop.

criteria: Checked against the provider's bill.

nodes.title: Everything runs on a laptop with no NVIDIA graphics card.

criteria: All runs and tests pass on the learner's MacBook Pro.

nodes.title: Each fish-tank and predator-prey training run takes ≤ 60 minutes per seed on the laptop's processor, or on rented hardware within QR-05.

criteria: Timed from the run's own elapsed-time log.

acceptance: Every contract type is code in its component's `types.py` (Protocols in `core/protocols.py`), with `core.Env` and `core.StepResult` keyed by team (`core.TeamSpec`, `core.SOLO`) and each team batch-first, `core.Transition` and `core.Agent` per team, and `core.ActionSpace` (AD-09, AD-13); each `tests/contracts/<id>.<Type>/` sample validates against its schema, and the `core.Agent`, `core.Env`, `runs.RunWriter` and `viz.Replay` replay doubles serve their recordings

Every step, contract function and entry function imports with its contract signature, its body `raise NotImplementedError("<task id>")`; the function fakes named on `**Boundary:**` lines serve their fixtures

Each component `__init__.py` exports only its contract; `src/rllab/lab/__main__.py` dispatches `train` (PL-01, or PL-02 when `agent = "reference"`), `eval`, `report` and `replay`, one entry call per seed or target
The `core.RunSettings` sample's TOML loads to an equal `RunSettings`; an unknown agent raises `ValueError` naming the key; `with_seed` swaps only the seed

nodes.title: runs store spine (one folder per run)

acceptance: A run written with `create_run` and `RunWriter` from the samples reads back through `open_run` as an equal `RunRecord`; a folder without `settings.json` raises `FileNotFoundError` naming the run

On the `core.RunSettings` samples, `make_env` returns a zero-argument factory of the named environment, and `make_agent` one agent per team (`{SOLO: agent}` for Snake and the corridor), sized from the team's `TeamSpec`, with the ablation switch from `settings.ablation`

On the `core.Transition` samples, the agent learns after `learn_start` from random batches of its memory, with a 128×128 MLP, a hard target refresh, Huber loss and gradient clip 10, on CPU in one thread; `act(explore=False)` is its argmax

On the `core.Env` and `core.Agent` replay doubles, `train` takes one agent per team, builds one batch-first `Transition` per learning team per step and calls its `learn`, adds a CurvePoint at step 0 and every `eval_every`, prints a progress line at least every 30 s, and saves a checkpoint and 5 recorded games

nodes.title: train_reference spine (library DQN on the adapter)

nodes.title: Each environment teaches one named RL concept, and I can explain, backed by my own runs, why the agent learns.
Algorithms I write from scratch are trustworthy: on the same environment, they perform about as well as a well-known library version.
Every trained agent clearly beats both a random player and a simple scripted player, measured over many games rather than judged by eye.
I can watch a replay of any trained agent playing.
A new environment reuses a shared core (environment interface, training loop, logging, replay viewer), so it only needs its own game and concept code.
A new game places a length-3 snake and one food on a 10×10 grid.

criteria: Given a new game, when it starts, then the snake has length 3, lies fully inside the grid, and the food is on a cell the snake does not occupy.

nodes.title: Each step takes one of three actions: go straight, turn left, or turn right, relative to the current heading.

criteria: Given the snake heading up, when the action is "turn left", then the head moves one cell left and the heading becomes left.

nodes.title: Moving onto the food grows the snake by 1 and adds 1 to the score.

criteria: Given the head next to the food, when it moves onto it, then length and score each increase by 1, and new food appears on an empty cell.

nodes.title: Moving into a wall or the snake's own body ends the game.

criteria: Given the head at the right edge heading right, when the action is "go straight", then the game is over.
Given the head next to its own body, when it moves into the body, then the game is over.

nodes.title: A game ends after 100 × current length steps without eating.

criteria: Given a length-3 snake that has not eaten for 299 steps, when it takes one more step without eating, then the game is over.

nodes.title: Rewards default to +1 for food, −1 for game over, and 0 otherwise. Each run can set its own values.

criteria: Given default settings, when the snake eats, then the reward is +1. When the game ends by collision or starvation, the reward is −1.
Given a run that sets food to +10, when the snake eats, then the reward is +10.

nodes.title: Games are reproducible from a seed.

criteria: Given the same seed and the same actions, when two games are played, then every snake position, food position and reward is identical.

nodes.title: The compact view gives 11 yes/no values: danger straight, left and right; heading (one of four); and whether the food is left, right, above or below the head.

criteria: Given a wall directly ahead and food above-right of the head, when the compact view is read, then "danger straight", "food right" and "food up" are yes, and the other danger and food values are no.

nodes.title: The full-grid view shows every cell's contents: empty, snake head, snake body, or food.

criteria: Given any game state, when the full-grid view is read, then exactly one cell is marked head, one is marked food, and the body cells match the snake's body.

nodes.title: The tank is a circle of radius 1. The ball (radius 0.08) moves 0.03 per step in a straight line and reflects off the wall at the angle it arrived, at unchanged speed.

criteria: Given the ball heading straight at the wall along a radius, when it reaches the wall, then it comes back along the same radius at speed 0.03.
Given the ball arriving at 30° to the wall's normal, when it reflects, then it leaves at 30° on the other side of the normal.

nodes.title: Each fish's action is a 2-D swim vector. A vector longer than 1 is shortened to length 1, then scaled by the fish's top speed of 0.024 per step (0.8 × the ball's speed).

criteria: Given the action (3, 4), when the fish moves, then it moves 0.024 in direction (0.6, 0.8).
Given the action (0.5, 0), when the fish moves, then it moves 0.012 in direction (1, 0).

nodes.title: A fish can't leave the tank. A move that would cross the wall stops at the wall.

criteria: Given a fish 0.01 inside the wall swimming straight outward at full speed, when it moves, then it ends on the wall, not beyond it.

nodes.title: A fish is caught when its centre comes within 0.11 of the ball's centre (ball radius 0.08 plus fish radius 0.03). It stops swimming, and its survival time is the number of steps it completed.

criteria: Given a fish 0.10 from the ball's centre after a step, when the step resolves, then that fish is caught with survival time equal to that step's number minus 1.

nodes.title: Each fish earns +1 for each step it survives and 0 on the step it is caught. Each run can set its own values.

criteria: Given default settings, when a fish survives a step, then its reward is +1.

nodes.title: A game ends when every fish is caught or after 1,000 steps. The game's score is the mean survival time per fish.

criteria: Given 8 fish of which 6 are caught at steps 100–600 and 2 survive, when step 1,000 is reached, then the game is truncated and the score is the mean of the 8 survival times, counting 1,000 for each survivor.

nodes.title: The number of fish is set per run, from 1 to 16; the school rungs use 8. Fish never collide and may overlap.

criteria: Given two fish swimming to the same point, when they arrive, then both occupy it and neither is blocked.

nodes.title: A new game places the ball at a random position with a random direction, and each fish at a random position at least 0.4 from the ball. The same seed and actions give the same game.

criteria: Given the same seed and the same actions, when two games are played, then every fish and ball position and every reward is identical.

nodes.title: The full view gives each fish 8 values: its own position and velocity, the ball's position relative to it, and the ball's velocity.

criteria: Given a fish at (0.5, 0) and the ball at (0, 0) moving (0.03, 0), when the fish's full view is read, then the ball's relative position is (−0.5, 0) and its velocity (0.03, 0).

nodes.title: The limited view gives each fish 9 values: its own position and velocity, a "ball visible" flag, and the ball's relative position and velocity. The ball counts as visible only within 0.5 of the fish; otherwise the flag is 0 and the ball values are 0. Fish never see other fish.

criteria: Given the ball 0.6 from a fish, when its limited view is read, then the flag and the four ball values are 0.
Given the ball 0.4 from the fish, when its limited view is read, then the flag is 1 and the ball values match the full view.

nodes.title: A game takes place in a tank of radius 1 with 1 predator, 6 prey and 8 pellets, and ends after 1,000 steps.

criteria: Given a new game, when it starts, then there are 1 predator, 6 prey and 8 pellets inside the tank, and step 1,000 truncates it.

nodes.title: Each animal's action is a 2-D swim vector, shortened to length 1 if longer, then scaled by its top speed: 0.024 per step for prey, 0.03 for the predator. Animals stop at the wall, as in FISH-03.

criteria: Given the predator's action (3, 4), when it moves, then it moves 0.03 in direction (0.6, 0.8).
Given a prey's action (3, 4), when it moves, then it moves 0.024 in direction (0.6, 0.8).

nodes.title: A prey whose centre comes within 0.05 of a pellet's centre eats it and earns +1. The pellet reappears at a random spot 20 steps later.

criteria: Given a prey 0.04 from a pellet after a step, when the step resolves, then the prey earns +1, the pellet is gone, and 20 steps later a pellet appears again.

nodes.title: The predator catches a prey whose centre comes within 0.08 of its own, earning +1 while the prey earns −5. A caught prey is out for 50 steps, then reappears at a random spot at least 0.4 from the predator.

criteria: Given a prey 0.07 from the predator after a step, when the step resolves, then the predator earns +1, the prey −5, and the prey is absent for the next 50 steps.
Given a caught prey's 50 steps are over, when it reappears, then it is at least 0.4 from the predator.

nodes.title: Each prey sees 18 values: its own position and velocity; a "visible" flag and the predator's relative position and velocity, only within 0.5; and, for its 3 nearest pellets within 0.5, a "visible" flag and the relative position of each. Anything out of range is 0 with its flag 0.

criteria: Given the predator 0.6 from a prey, when the prey's view is read, then the predator flag and its four values are 0.

nodes.title: The predator sees 19 values: its own position and velocity, and, for its 3 nearest swimming prey within 0.6, a "visible" flag and the relative position and velocity of each.

criteria: Given only one prey within 0.6, when the predator's view is read, then one prey slot is filled and the other two are 0 with their flags 0.

nodes.title: The predator and the prey are two teams. Each team has its own view and its own policy, and a step takes one action per animal from each team.

criteria: Given a step, when both teams act, then the predator's action comes from the predator team's policy and every prey's from the prey team's policy.

nodes.title: The predator's score is catches per game. The prey's score is the mean total reward per prey per game.

criteria: Given a game with 4 catches and prey rewards summing to 12, when it ends, then the predator scores 4 and the prey score 2.0.

nodes.title: A new game places the prey and pellets at random spots at least 0.4 from the predator. The same seed and actions give the same game.

criteria: Given the same seed and the same actions, when two games are played, then every position, reward and catch is identical.

nodes.title: The random player picks each of the three actions with equal chance.

criteria: Given 30,000 random-player steps, when the actions are counted, then each action's share is between 32% and 35%.

nodes.title: The scripted player steps toward the food if that move is safe. Otherwise it takes any safe move. If no move is safe, it goes straight.

criteria: Given food directly ahead and no danger ahead, when the scripted player moves, then it goes straight.
Given food to the left but danger to the left, and the right is safe, when it moves, then it turns right.

nodes.title: Baselines are evaluated with the same protocol as agents (EVAL-01).

criteria: Given an evaluation report, when it is read, then it lists both baselines' scores next to every agent's.

nodes.title: The random swimmer picks each fish's swim vector uniformly from the disc of radius 1.

criteria: Given 30,000 random-swimmer actions, when their lengths are counted, then between 23% and 27% are shorter than 0.5.

nodes.title: The scripted fish swims at full speed directly away from the ball's centre, using the full view.

criteria: Given the ball at (0, 0) and a fish at (0.3, 0.4), when the scripted fish acts, then its action is (0.6, 0.8) at length 1.
Given the ball exactly on the fish's centre, when it acts, then it swims toward the tank's centre or, at the centre, along (1, 0).

nodes.title: The scripted predator swims at full speed toward its nearest visible prey, otherwise toward the tank's centre.

criteria: Given a visible prey at relative position (0.3, 0.4), when the scripted predator acts, then its action is (0.6, 0.8).
Given no visible prey, when it acts at (0.5, 0), then it swims toward (0, 0).

nodes.title: A scripted prey flees at full speed directly away from the predator when it is within 0.3, and otherwise swims at full speed to its nearest visible pellet. With neither, it stays still.

criteria: Given the predator at relative position (0.12, 0.16), when the scripted prey acts, then its action is (−0.6, −0.8).
Given the predator out of range and a pellet at relative position (0.3, 0), when it acts, then its action is (1, 0).

nodes.title: The random predator and random prey draw each swim vector uniformly from the disc of radius 1, as BASE-04 does.

criteria: Given 30,000 random-predator actions, when their lengths are counted, then between 23% and 27% are shorter than 0.5.

nodes.title: The table-based agent keeps one learned value per compact-view situation and action. It updates that value after every step, from the reward plus its estimate of the next situation.

criteria: Given a step that earns +1 food reward, when the agent updates, then the value for that situation and action moves toward the reward.

nodes.title: While training, each agent sometimes takes a random action instead of its best one. That chance falls over training to a set minimum.

criteria: Given a run's exploration settings, when training reaches the end of the decay period, then the random-action rate equals the set minimum.

nodes.title: The compact-view neural agent learns from batches drawn at random from a memory of past steps.

criteria: Given a full memory, when a training batch is drawn, then it holds steps from more than one game.

nodes.title: The compact-view neural agent computes its learning targets from a separate copy of itself. That copy is refreshed only at set intervals.

criteria: Given a refresh interval of N steps, when fewer than N steps have passed since the last refresh, then the target copy is unchanged.

nodes.title: The full-grid neural agent learns from the full-grid view, using the same memory and target-copy behavior as AGENT-03 and AGENT-04.

criteria: Given a full-grid run, when training starts, then the agent receives only the full-grid view, never the compact view.

nodes.title: The lab's own agents, value learners and policy-gradient learners alike, are written from basic array and tensor operations, including automatic gradients. They contain no reinforcement learning library code.

criteria: Given the agents' code, when it is reviewed, then it uses no reinforcement learning library.

nodes.title: During evaluation, agents never explore. Value learners take their best-valued action, and policy learners take their policy's mean action.

criteria: Given an evaluation game, when the agent acts, then no action is random.

nodes.title: The policy maps each observation to a Gaussian over the 2-D swim vector: a mean from a neural network, and a learned spread. Training samples actions from it.

criteria: Given any observation, when the policy acts during training, then the action is drawn from the Gaussian, and its log-probability is available for learning.

nodes.title: The plain policy-gradient agent updates after each batch of whole games. Each action is pushed toward or away from in proportion to the discounted return from that step, normalised within the batch.

criteria: Given a batch where one action led to a higher return than the batch mean, when the agent updates, then that action's log-probability rises.

nodes.title: The clipped policy-gradient agent learns from batches of steps. It estimates each step's advantage with a learned value estimate, then updates for several passes with an objective that clips the policy's change to within 0.2 of its previous probability ratio.

criteria: Given a batch whose new-to-old probability ratio exceeds 1.2 for a step with positive advantage, when the objective is computed, then that step contributes no further gain beyond the 1.2 ratio.

nodes.title: In a school, one shared policy acts for each fish independently from that fish's own view, and every fish's experience trains it.

criteria: Given a school of 8, when one step is taken, then the policy is queried once per swimming fish, and each fish's step enters the same training batch.

nodes.title: Each rung's settings fix its game, fish count, view and agent, so the four rungs are reproducible runs like any other.

criteria: Given the rung-3 settings, when a run starts, then it trains a shared clipped policy-gradient policy on 8 fish with the full view.

nodes.title: Each learning team uses its own clipped policy-gradient agent (PG-03); in a co-learning run both teams learn at once.

criteria: Given a rung-2 run, when it trains, then the predator and prey policies are updated from their own teams' experience only.

nodes.title: Rung 1 is two runs, each training one team against the other team's scripted player.

criteria: Given the rung-1 prey settings, when the run trains, then the predator is the scripted predator throughout.

nodes.title: In rung 3, each game's opponent for a team is the other team's latest policy with probability 0.5, and otherwise one of its saved past generations, chosen uniformly.

criteria: Given 1,000 rung-3 games after generation 5, when the opponents are counted, then the latest policy is chosen in 45%–55% of them, and every earlier generation appears.

nodes.title: A learning run saves each learning team's policy every tenth of its step budget, giving 10 generations per team.

criteria: Given a finished co-learning run, when its record is opened, then each team has 10 numbered generations.

nodes.title: A cross-play table pits every predator generation against every prey generation of a run: 50 games per pairing on held-out seeds, recording both teams' scores.

criteria: Given a co-learning run's 10 generations per team, when cross-play runs, then the table has 100 cells of 50 games each.

nodes.title: Each generation's rating is its mean score against all of the other team's generations in the cross-play table.

criteria: Given a cross-play table, when ratings are computed, then each predator generation's rating is the mean of its row, and each prey generation's the mean of its column.

nodes.title: The fixed panel for a team is the other team's scripted player, its random player, and the final trained policy from the other team's rung-1 run.

criteria: Given the panel for the prey team, when it is listed, then it holds the scripted predator, the random predator and the rung-1 predator.

nodes.title: An evaluation plays 200 games for each of 5 training seeds, on evaluation seeds never used in training. It reports the mean score and its spread. In every environment, scripted and random players are measured the same way.

criteria: Given a trained agent, when it is evaluated, then 1,000 games are played and the report shows the mean score and spread for each seed and overall.

nodes.title: Every agent in every environment significantly beats that environment's random player. This is tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill on the EVAL-01 scores, and passes only if significant at 5% after correcting for the number of comparisons.

criteria: Given Snake's three agents and the random player's scores, when tested, then each agent's corrected result is significant at 5%.
Given the four fish-tank rungs and the random swimmer's scores, when tested, then each rung's corrected result is significant at 5%.
Given each learned predator-prey team and its own side's random player, both playing against the same scripted opposition, when tested, then each corrected result is significant at 5%.

criteria: Given both players' EVAL-01 scores, when tested for "agent worse than scripted", then the result is not significant.

nodes.title: At least one agent significantly beats the scripted player, tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill at 5% after correction.

criteria: Given all three agents' EVAL-01 scores, when each is tested against the scripted player, then at least one corrected result is significant.

nodes.title: The report states, as stretch targets that are not pass conditions, whether Snake's full-grid agent beats the scripted player and whether the limited-view school beats the scripted fish.

criteria: Given either agent's scores, when the report is produced, then it shows that test's result and labels it "stretch".

nodes.title: Each agent's learning curve shows evaluation score against training steps, with the two baseline means drawn as reference lines.

criteria: Given a finished run, when its curve is shown, then both baseline lines appear on the same chart.

nodes.title: The full-view clipped rungs (2 and 3) each significantly beat the scripted fish, tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill at 5% after correction.

criteria: Given each rung's and the scripted fish's EVAL-01 scores, when tested, then each corrected result is significant.

nodes.title: The single-fish clipped agent (rung 2) significantly beats the single-fish plain agent (rung 1), with the same step budget and seeds, tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill at 5% after correction.

criteria: Given both rungs' EVAL-01 scores, when tested for "rung 2 greater than rung 1", then the corrected result is significant.

nodes.title: Each rung-1 predator-prey team significantly beats its own side's scripted player against the same scripted opposition, tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill at 5% after correction.

criteria: Given the rung-1 predator and the scripted predator, each against scripted prey, when tested for "learned greater than scripted" on catches, then the corrected result is significant; likewise for the rung-1 prey and scripted prey against the scripted predator.

nodes.title: Each team's rung-3 final policy significantly beats that team's rung-2 final policy against its fixed panel (SELF-07), pooled over the panel's opponents, tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill at 5% after correction.

criteria: Given both rungs' final predators against the predator's panel, when tested for "rung 3 greater than rung 2", then the corrected result is significant; likewise for the prey.

nodes.title: The report shows rung 2's and rung 3's cross-play tables and each team's ratings by generation. Rung 2's are labelled "reported", not a pass condition.

criteria: Given a finished predator-prey report, when it is read, then both rungs' tables and rating charts appear, and rung 2's carry the "reported" label.

nodes.title: For each environment, the reference implementation trains on the compared rung's setup: the same game, view, agent counts, opponent, rewards, number of training steps and training seeds. It is evaluated with EVAL-01.

criteria: Given a reference run, when its settings are compared with the compared rung's, then game, view, fish count, rewards, steps and seeds match.

nodes.title: The compared rung's mean score is at least 90% of the reference's mean score.

criteria: Given both EVAL-01 results, when compared, then agent mean ≥ 0.9 × reference mean.

nodes.title: The compared rung is not significantly worse than the reference, tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill at 5% after correction.

criteria: Given both EVAL-01 score sets, when tested for "agent worse than reference", then the result is not significant.

nodes.title: The compact-view neural agent can run with no memory, learning only from its most recent step.

criteria: Given the no-memory switch, when training, then each update uses only the latest step.

nodes.title: The compact-view neural agent can run with no separate target copy, computing targets from itself.

criteria: Given the no-target-copy switch, when training, then the targets come from the current agent at every step.

nodes.title: The table-based agent can run with no exploration, always taking its best-valued action.

criteria: Given the no-exploration switch, when training, then no action is random.

criteria: Given a finished ablation, when the comparison is shown, then both curves share one chart and the report gives each one's EVAL-01 mean.

nodes.title: A run is fully described by its settings: environment and its own settings (such as fish count), view, agent, rewards, exploration where the agent uses it, step budget and seed.

criteria: Given a settings description, when a run is launched from it, then no other input is needed.

criteria: Given a finished run, when its record is opened, then its settings, seed, curve, final checkpoints and recorded games are present.
Given a finished co-learning run, when its record is opened, then each team's 10 generations are present.

nodes.title: The same settings and seed on the same machine produce the same learning curve.

criteria: Given two runs with identical settings and seed, when their curves are compared, then they match exactly.

nodes.title: During training, progress is shown at least every 30 seconds: steps, games, recent mean score, and elapsed time.

criteria: Given a running training job, when 30 seconds pass, then a progress line has appeared.

nodes.title: A saved checkpoint can be reloaded and evaluated without retraining.

criteria: Given a finished run's checkpoint, when it is evaluated, then the scores match the run's own evaluation.

nodes.title: Any recorded game from any saved run can be played back, showing the board (Snake's grid, the corridor, or the tank with the ball and every fish, caught fish marked), the score and the step number.

criteria: Given a saved run, when one of its games is replayed, then each frame matches the recorded game state.

nodes.title: Playback can be paused, stepped one frame at a time, and sped up or slowed down.

criteria: Given a paused replay, when "step" is pressed, then exactly one frame advances.

nodes.title: New games can be recorded from any saved checkpoint, or in predator-prey from any pairing of a predator and a prey checkpoint or generation, and then replayed.

criteria: Given a checkpoint and a seed, when games are recorded, then they can be replayed like any other recorded game.
Given prey generation 2 and predator generation 9 of a run, when a game is recorded, then it replays like any other.

nodes.title: Every environment offers the same two operations, and declares its teams: each team's agents, observation shape, and whether its actions are discrete or continuous. Starting a game from a seed returns one observation per agent of each team. Taking a step, with one action per active agent of each team, returns each agent's next observation and reward, which agents are done, whether the game is over, and extra information.

criteria: Given Snake (one team, one agent, discrete), the fish tank (one team, 8 agents, continuous) or predator-prey (a 1-agent and a 6-agent team, continuous), when a game is started and stepped, then all return the same kinds of result.

nodes.title: The corridor is a row of 10 cells. The agent starts at the left end and moves left or right. Reaching the right end gives +1 and ends the game. A game also ends after 50 steps.

criteria: Given the agent at cell 9 of 10, when it moves right, then the reward is +1 and the game is over.
Given the agent at the left end, when it moves left, then it stays in place.

nodes.title: The table-based agent, trained on the corridor through the core, reaches the right end in ≥ 95% of evaluation games, in at most 12 steps.

criteria: Given a trained corridor agent, when evaluated, then ≥ 95% of games reach the right end within 12 steps.

nodes.title: Adding the corridor needs no change to the shared core.

criteria: Given the core as Snake uses it, when the corridor is added, then the change touches only corridor code.

nodes.title: Snake and the corridor behave exactly as before after the core's interface revision.

criteria: Given a seed and an action sequence recorded before the revision, when they are replayed after it, then every observation, reward and game end is identical.
